newsitem.title: USA: Levi Strauss to recall some fleece garments.
newsitem.headline: Levi Strauss to recall some fleece garments.

text.p: Levi Strauss & Co said today that in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, it will recall about 57,000 shirts, made with a fleece fabric called sherpa, over concerns about their potential for catching fire.

The privately-held company said it is recalling over 34,000 Levi's Jeans for Women junior-sized sweatshirts that failed to meet federal mandatory standards for fabric flammability, may ignite readily, and present a serious risk of burn injuries in violation of the federal Flammable Fabrics Act.

Fabrics that do not comply with the standard, said the company, typically burn faster than newspaper. Both CPSC and Levi Strauss said they are not aware of any injuries involving these shirts and that the recall is being conducted to prevent the possibility of injury.
The company also said it is also voluntarily recalling about 23,000 similar sweatshirts, which may fail the federal mandatory standards for fabric flammability, sold under the
Dockers Khakis for Women label and the Dockers Authentics for Men label.
Levi Strauss it is aware of one incident of these shirts a reportedly flaring up when exposed to a flame, but no injuries resulted.
The CPSC said it is continuing to investigate additional fleece garments to determine whether or not they are in compliance with the law.
